notes: FLSA has no daily overtime, meal-break, rest-break, minimum-rest-between-shifts, predictive-scheduling, or reporting-time-pay requirement for adults.
FLSA sets no hours or time-of-day limits for 16- and 17-year-olds in non-agricultural work; only hazardous-occupation orders apply to them.
minor_limits school_week=true: 'max_hours_day' is for days school is in session; 'max_hours_non_school_day' (extra key) is the cap on a non-school day within a school week (29 CFR 570.35(a)(1),(3)).

Tipped minimum wage: max_tip_credit_per_hour 5.12 = $7.25 federal minimum wage − $2.13 cash wage (29 CFR 531.50(a)(2)); tip credit only for employees who customarily receive more than $30/month in tips and only after notice to the employee.

Hazardous orders mapped to ROLE_TAGS (29 CFR Part 570, re-read from eCFR 2026-11-07): HO 2 motor_vehicle_driving, HO 7 powered_industrial_truck, HO 10 meat_slicer, HO 11 bakery_machine, HO 12 baler_compactor, HO 14 power_saw. Each order covers 'minors between 16 and 18', and 570.33(b) extends every order to 14-15, so the rules use age_below 18 with no age_min. Exemptions not modeled (the tag bans the role outright, conservative): 17-year-old occasional and incidental driving (570.52(b): <= 6,000 lb GVW, daylight only, valid license and driver ed, no moving violations, no towing/route/urgent deliveries such as pizza, <= 2 delivery trips/day, <= 30 miles, <= 1/3 of the workday and 20% of the workweek); 16-17 loading (not operating or unloading) of ANSI-compliant scrap paper balers and paper box compactors with a key-lock switch held by adults 18+ and a posted notice (570.63(c)(1)); household-type countertop mixers (not hardwired, <= 1/2 hp, <= 5 qt bowl) and fully guarded pizza-dough rollers (570.62(b)), also carved out of HO 10 when not processing meat or poultry (570.61(a)(4)); apprentices and student-learners (570.50(b),(c)) under HO 10, 12 and 14.

14-15 (570.33-.34): US.minor_prohibited_roles.7 cooking/fryer, .8 ladder_scaffold, .9 power-driven machinery, hoisting and driving. Permitted cooking is only electric/gas grills with no open flame and deep fryers that automatically lower and raise the baskets (570.34(c)); rotisseries, broilers and pressurized equipment including fryolators are not permitted. 'cooking' and 'fryer' are banned outright for 14-15 because a role tag cannot say which equipment is used (conservative: an auto-basket fryer or flameless grill would be lawful). 570.33(e) bans 14-15 from all power-driven machinery (food slicers, grinders, choppers, processors, mixers, with no small-mixer carve-out) except office machines, vacuums and floor waxers; dishwashers, toasters, milkshake blenders and coffee machines are permitted (570.34(i)). Rules start at age_min 14 because 570.2(a)(1) sets a general 16-year minimum and subpart C permits only 14-15 (no non-agricultural work is authorized under 14). 570.2(a)(2) exempts employment by a parent of their own child from the 14-15 rules (not from the hazardous orders); not modeled.
No federal age rule for alcohol_service (state law governs).

rules.summary: Non-exempt employees get 1.5x their regular rate for hours over 40 in a workweek.

citation.title: 29 U.S.C. § 207(a)(1) — Maximum hours
citation.excerpt: for a workweek longer than forty hours ... at a rate not less than one and one-half times the regular rate

rules.summary: The federal minimum wage is $7.25 an hour.

citation.title: 29 U.S.C. § 206(a)(1)(C) — Minimum wage
citation.excerpt: $7.25 an hour, beginning 24 months after that 60th day (i.e. July 24, 2009)

rules.summary: In a school week, 14- and 15-year-olds may work at most 3 hours on a school day (8 on a non-school day), 18 hours total, between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.35(a) — Hours of work for minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: Not more than 3 hours in any 1 day when school is in session ... Not more than 18 hours in any 1 week when school is in session

rules.summary: When school is not in session, 14- and 15-year-olds may work up to 8 hours a day and 40 a week, 7 a.m.-7 p.m. (9 p.m. from June 1 through Labor Day).

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.35(a) — Hours of work for minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: Between 7 a.m. and 7 p.m. ... except during the summer (June 1 through Labor Day) when the evening hour will be 9 p.m.

rules.summary: Workers under 18 may not operate or ride on forklifts and other high-lift trucks (Hazardous Occupations Order No. 7).

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.58 — Power-driven hoisting apparatus (HO 7)
citation.excerpt: operating, tending, riding upon ... high-lift truck ... highlift trucks known under such names as fork lifts, fork trucks, fork lift trucks

rules.summary: Under the FLSA an employer may pay tipped employees a cash wage of $2.13 an hour and count up to $5.12 of tips toward the $7.25 minimum wage.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 531.50 — Statutory provisions with respect to tipped employees (FLSA § 3(m)(2)(A))
citation.excerpt: The cash wage paid such employee which ... shall not be less than the cash wage required to be paid such an employee on August 20, 1996 [ i.e., $2.13]

rules.summary: Workers under 18 may not operate, feed, set up or clean power-driven meat slicers and similar food-processing machines, including deli slicers for meat, cheese or bread (HO 10).

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.61(a)(4) — Power-driven meat-processing machines (HO 10)
citation.excerpt: regardless of the product being processed by these machines (including, for example, the slicing in a retail delicatessen of meat, poultry, seafood, bread, vegetables, or cheese, etc.): meat patty forming machines ... meat slicers

rules.summary: Workers under 18 may not operate or clean power-driven bakery machines such as dough and batter mixers and dough sheeters (HO 11); small household-type countertop mixers and guarded pizza-dough rollers are exempt.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.62 — Bakery machines (HO 11)
citation.excerpt: operating, assisting to operate, or setting up, adjusting, repairing, oiling, or cleaning any horizontal or vertical dough mixer; batter mixer; bread dividing, rounding, or molding machine; dough brake; dough sheeter

rules.summary: Workers under 18 may not operate or unload balers and paper box compactors (HO 12); 16- and 17-year-olds may only load ANSI-compliant, key-locked machines that cannot run while loading.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.63 — Balers, compactors, and paper-products machines (HO 12)
citation.excerpt: particularly hazardous for the employment of minors between 16 and 18 years of age: (1) The occupations of operation or assisting to operate ... scrap paper baler, paper box compactor

rules.summary: Workers under 18 may not drive on public roads for work (HO 2); 17-year-olds may drive only incidentally under strict conditions (daylight, <= 6,000 lb, no route deliveries).

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.52 — Motor-vehicle driver and outside helper (HO 2)
citation.excerpt: the occupations of motor-vehicle driver and outside helper on any public road, highway ... are particularly hazardous for the employment of minors between 16 and 18 years of age

rules.summary: Workers under 18 may not operate or help on circular saws, band saws, guillotine shears, chain saws, reciprocating saws, wood chippers or abrasive cutting discs, or set up or clean them (HO 14).

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.65 — Circular saws, band saws, guillotine shears, etc. (HO 14)
citation.excerpt: The occupations of operator of or helper on the following power-driven fixed or portable machines except machines equipped with full automatic feed and ejection: (i) Circular saws. (ii) Band saws. (iii) Guillotine shears.

rules.summary: 14- and 15-year-olds may not cook or bake, except on electric or gas grills with no open flame and on deep fryers that lower and raise the baskets automatically; no broilers, rotisseries or pressure fryers.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.33(h) and § 570.34(c) — Cooking by minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: All baking and cooking activities except that cooking which is permitted by § 570.34(c) ... Cooking is also permitted with deep fryers ... which automatically lowers the baskets into the hot oil

rules.summary: 14- and 15-year-olds may not do any work that requires ladders, scaffolds or their substitutes.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.33(g) — Occupations prohibited to minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: all work requiring the use of ladders, scaffolds, or their substitutes

rules.summary: 14- and 15-year-olds may not operate, clean or set up any power-driven machinery (including food slicers, grinders and mixers of any size), hoisting equipment such as forklifts, or motor vehicles.

citation.title: 29 CFR § 570.33(c), (e), (f) — Occupations prohibited to minors 14 and 15
citation.excerpt: operating, tending, setting up, adjusting, cleaning, oiling, or repairing any power-driven machinery, including ... food slicers, food grinders, food choppers, food processors, food cutters, and food mixers ... (f) The operation of motor vehicles
